full_judgment: 6. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the State submits that the doctor who held post-mortem examination found so many injuries on the person of the deceased and the ligature in the neck was found to be post-mortem in nature and that the doctor opined that the death was due to shock and haemorrhage as a result of the injuries which were ante-mortem and homicidal in nature and this indicates that deceased Rozina Khatun was done to death and as she was living with her husband on the date of occurrence it can be presumed that the husband was responsible for the commission of murder. The learned Advocate contends that by suggesting that the deceased committed suicide by hanging the appellant tried to save himself from being punished. As the wife was murdered while in custody of the husband the natural presumption is that the husband is responsible for the death of the wife. The learned advocate in support of her contention placed reliance in the case of State Vs. Kalu Bepari 43 DLR 249 and 42 DLR 440 (Rezaul Huq & ors. Vs. State).
